The eighth season of the American [[television comedy]] ''[[The Office (American TV series)|The Office]]'' commenced airing on [[NBC]] in the United States on September 22, 2011, and concluded on May 10, 2012, consisting of 24 episodes. The series is an American adaptation of the [[The Office (British TV series)|British comedy series of the same name]], and is presented in a [[mockumentary]] format, portraying the daily lives of office employees in the Scranton, Pennsylvania branch of the fictitious [[Dunder Mifflin Paper Company]]. The eighth season of ''The Office'' aired on Thursdays at 9:00&nbsp;p.m. ([[Eastern Time Zone (North America)|Eastern]]) in the United States as part of the "[[Comedy Night Done Right]]" television block. It stars [[Rainn Wilson]], [[John Krasinski]], [[Jenna Fischer]], [[B. J. Novak]], [[Ed Helms]], and [[James Spader]], with supporting performances from [[Catherine Tate]], [[Leslie David Baker]], [[Brian Baumgartner]], [[Creed Bratton]], [[Kate Flannery]], [[Mindy Kaling]], [[Ellie Kemper]], [[Angela Kinsey]], [[Paul Lieberstein]], [[Oscar Nunez]], [[Craig Robinson (actor)|Craig Robinson]], [[Phyllis Smith]], and [[Zach Woods]]. This was the first season without [[Steve Carell]] as [[Michael Scott (The Office)|Michael Scott]] in the lead role and the only one to not feature the character in any onscreen capacity, although he is occasionally mentioned.

The eighth season largely centers on [[Andy Bernard]]'s ([[Ed Helms]]) ascension to regional manager, as well as the antics of [[Robert California]] ([[James Spader]]), the new CEO of Sabre, a fictional printer company that owns [[Dunder Mifflin]]. Halfway through the season, [[Dwight Schrute]] ([[Rainn Wilson]])—along with [[Jim Halpert]] ([[John Krasinski]]), [[Stanley Hudson]] ([[Leslie David Baker]]), [[Ryan Howard (The Office)|Ryan Howard]] ([[B. J. Novak]]), [[Erin Hannon]] ([[Ellie Kemper]]), and [[Cathy Simms]] ([[Lindsey Broad]])—travel to Florida to help set up a Sabre Store, where [[Nellie Bertram]] ([[Catherine Tate]]) is introduced. Eventually, former CFO of Dunder Mifflin [[David Wallace (The Office)|David Wallace]] ([[Andy Buckley]]) buys back the company, firing California.

Despite debuting with moderate viewing figures, the departure of Carell affected the show's ratings, which fell as the season progressed. The season ranked as the eighty-seventh-most watched television series during the [[2011–12 United States network television schedule|2011–12 television year]] and saw a dramatic decrease in ratings from [[The Office (American season 7)|the previous season]]. Critical reception was polarized. Many critics argued that the series should have ended after the departure of Carell; many also felt that the season recycled storylines from past episodes. Other critics were more positive, complimenting various actors and their characters. It marked the first time since [[The Office (American season 1)|season one]] that the show received no [[Emmy Award|Emmy nominations]].

==Production==
The eighth season of ''The Office'' was the last season of the show to be produced by [[Universal Media Studios]] and [[Endemol Shine North America|Reveille Productions]] before the companies were renamed "[[Universal Television]]" and "Shine America", respectively. It was also produced by [[Deedle-Dee Productions]].<ref name=season8dvd>{{cite AV media notes |title=The Office: The Complete Eighth Season |last=Novak|first=B. J.|type=DVD |publisher=[[NBC]]|display-authors=etal|year=2012}}</ref> The show is based on the [[The Office (British TV series)|British comedy series of the same name]], which was created by [[Ricky Gervais]] and [[Stephen Merchant]] for the British Broadcasting Corporation ([[BBC]]).<ref name=office-original/><ref name="GreenLight">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2004/may/18/broadcasting.internationalnews|title=American Office Gets Green Light|work=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=December 18, 2025}}</ref> This season of ''The Office'' was produced by [[Greg Daniels]] and [[Paul Lieberstein]]{{emdash}}the latter of whom served as the [[showrunner]].<ref name="GreenLight" /><ref>{{cite web|last=Schneider |first=Michael |url=https://variety.com/2008/scene/markets-festivals/aziz-ansari-hired-for-office-spinoff-1117987409/ |title=Aziz Ansari Hired for 'Office' Spinoff |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=June 12, 2011 |access-date=November 6, 2011}}</ref> Returning writers from the previous season included Lieberstein, [[Charlie Grandy]], [[Justin Spitzer]], [[Carrie Kemper]], [[Daniel Chun]], Robert Padnick, [[Aaron Shure]], [[Steve Hely]], [[Amelie Gillette]], [[Mindy Kaling]], and [[B. J. Novak]]; the latter two were both also credited as executive producers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2010/tv/news/novak-keeps-his-office-job-1118021972/|title=Novak Keeps His 'Office' Job|author=Cynthia Littleton|work=Variety|access-date=July 22, 2010|date=July 20, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Moaba |first=Alex |url=http://www.aoltv.com/2011/09/15/mindy-kaling-gets-office-promotion-to-executive-producer/ |title=Mindy Kaling Gets 'Office' Promotion to Executive Producer |publisher=AOL TV |date=September 15, 2011 |access-date=November 22, 2011 |archive-date=October 6, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191006051046/http://www.aoltv.com/2011/09/15/mindy-kaling-gets-office-promotion-to-executive-producer/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> It was previously unknown whether Kaling would write for the series any longer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aoltv.com/2011/05/12/mindy-kaling-the-office/|title=Is Mindy Kaling Done Writing for 'The Office'?|publisher=AOL TV|first=Joel|last=Keller|date=May 12, 2011|access-date=June 20, 2011|archive-date=December 25, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181225175334/http://www.aoltv.com/2011/05/12/mindy-kaling-the-office/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Kaling herself confirmed via her Twitter page that she would write the Christmas-themed episode, "[[Christmas Wishes (The Office)|Christmas Wishes]]", which was the last episode to use the "Universal Media Studios" logo.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/mindykaling/statuses/118831807075598337|title=I'm at home writing Office Christmas episode. I've eaten two gluten free donuts, now listening to Charlie Brown Christmas. It's sad here.|work=Twitter|last=Kaling|first=Mindy|date=September 27, 2011|access-date=September 28, 2011}}</ref> Three new writers joined the staff beginning in season eight: Owen Ellickson, [[Allison Silverman]] and [[Dan Greaney]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2011/06/staffing-season-highlights-who-got-hottest-jobs-which-shows-attracted-most-writers-139381/|title=Staffing Season Highlights: Who Got Hottest Jobs, Which Shows Attracted Most Writers|website=Deadline Hollywood|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=June 21, 2011|access-date=September 16, 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241202153737/https://deadline.com/2011/06/staffing-season-highlights-who-got-hottest-jobs-which-shows-attracted-most-writers-139381/|archive-date=December 2, 2024}}</ref> The season also saw the directorial debuts of cast members [[Ed Helms]] and [[Brian Baumgartner]]; Helms directed the episodes "Christmas Wishes" and "Welcome Party" and Baumgartner directed "[[After Hours (The Office)|After Hours]]".<ref name="trivia">{{cite web|url=http://www.officetally.com/the-office-season-8-spoilers-and-news|title=The Office Season 8 spoilers and news|publisher=OfficeTally|access-date=December 12, 2011}}</ref>

J. Novak Takes an ''Office'' Breather |work=[[TV Guide]] |first=Michael |last=Schneider |date=June 27, 2012 |access-date=June 27, 2012}}</ref> It was also Kaling's final full season, due to her pilot, ''[[The Mindy Project]]'', being picked up by [[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]].<ref>{{cite news|last=O'Neal |first=Sean |url=https://www.avclub.com/today-in-potential-omens-of-the-offices-demise-mindy-k-1798229564 |title=Today in Potential Omens of ''The Office''{{'}}s Demise: Mindy Kaling Attached to Star in a New Fox Series |newspaper=[[The A.V. Club]] |date=January 30, 2012 |access-date=February 5, 2012}}</ref> On February 28, 2012, it was announced that Spader would not return for a ninth season of the show.<ref>{{cite web|last=Sacks|first=Ethan|title=James Spader Leaving 'The Office' at Season's End|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/entertainment/television/james-spader-leaving-office-season-article-1.1029840|work=New York Daily News|date=February 28, 2012|access-date=February 29, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160409165726/http://www.nydailynews.com/entertainment/tv/james-spader-leaving-office-season-article-1.1029840|archive-date=April 9, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> There was initial speculation that following the eighth season, Daniels was considering rebooting the series due to the possible departures of main cast members.<ref name="office2.0"/> However, a new deal was negotiated with NBC, and all the main cast members{{emdash}}sans Spader, Novak, and Kaling{{emdash}}would return for the ninth season; NBC also announced that Catherine Tate would become a series regular.<ref name="fitz">{{cite web|last=Fitzpatrick|first=Kevin|title='The Office' Season 9 Casts a New Series Regular|url=https://screencrush.com/the-office-catherine-tate/|publisher=Screen Crush|access-date=June 6, 2012|date=June 1, 2012}}</ref><ref name="cindonna">{{cite web|last=West|first=Kelly|title=The Office Makes Catherine Tate A Series Regular For Season 9|url=https://www.cinemablend.com/television/Office-Makes-Catherine-Tate-Series-Regular-Season-9-43115.html|publisher=Cinema Blend|access-date=June 6, 2012|date=June 1, 2012}}</ref>

==Cast==
{{see also|List of The Office (American TV series) characters}}
''The Office'' employs an [[ensemble cast]]. Most of the main characters, and some supporting ones, are based on characters from the British version of ''The Office''. While these characters normally have the same attitudes and perceptions as their British counterparts, the roles have been redesigned to better fit the American show. The show is known for its large cast size, many of whom are known particularly for their [[improvisation]]al work.<ref name=office-original>{{cite web |last1=Gilbert |first1=Holly |title=The Office US Vs. UK Versions: Differences Explained |url=https://screenrant.com/office-us-vs-uk-versions-differences-explained/ |website=[[Screen Rant]] |access-date=December 18, 2025 |date=November 1, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Fotis|first=Matt|title=Fifty Key Improv Performers: Actors, Troupes, and Schools from Theatre, Film, and TV|publisher=[[Routledge]]|location=[[London]]|isbn=9781040113981|quote=''The Office'' incorporated improv into the show. The talking head interviews almost always featured improvised takes by the cast members, and they filmed many of the scripted scenes multiple times to allow for improvisation.|section=31. Steve Carell and Stephen Colbert}}</ref>

===Main===
* [[Rainn Wilson]] as [[Dwight Schrute]], based upon [[Gareth Keenan]], who is the office's top-performing sales representative. 
* [[John Krasinski]] as [[Jim Halpert]], a sales representative and prankster, who is based upon [[Tim Canterbury]], and is married to [[Pam Beesly|Pam Halpert]], the office administrator. 
* [[Jenna Fischer]] as [[Pam Beesly|Pam Halpert]], who is based on [[Dawn Tinsley]], is shy, but is often a cohort with Jim in his pranks on Dwight. She is pregnant during the first episodes of the season and leaves midway through the season.  
* [[B. J. Novak]] as [[Ryan Howard (The Office)|Ryan Howard]], a [[temporary worker]], who is based on Ricky Howard and [[Neil Godwin]].<ref>[https://www.comingsoon.net/news.php?id=3307  Hawaii, ''The Office'' & Lost in Space Castings] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120120220613/http://www.comingsoon.net/news.php?id=3307 |date=2012-01-20 }} ''Variety'', Retrieved April 13, 2008</ref> 
* [[Ed Helms]] as [[Andy Bernard]], the newly promoted manager—who was previously a salesman—and boastful Cornell alumnus whose love for [[a cappella]] music and awkward social skills generates mixed feelings from his employees.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nbcumv.com/mediavillage/networks/nbcentertainment/theoffice|title=The Office HOME|publisher=NBCUniversal Media Village|access-date=December 12, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111128222451/http://www.nbcumv.com/mediavillage/networks/nbcentertainment/theoffice|archive-date=November 28, 2011}}</ref> Andy is an original character, meaning he has no English equivalent from Gervais's series. 
* [[James Spader]] as [[Robert California]], the eccentric CEO of Sabre. Spader reprises his guest-starring role from the seventh season, and joined the regular cast to replace [[Kathy Bates]]'s character.<ref name="jamesspader">{{cite magazine |url=http://insidetv.ew.com/2011/07/06/james-spader-office/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110709072248/http://insidetv.ew.com/2011/07/06/james-spader-office/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 9, 2011 |title=Done Deal! James Spader joins 'The Office' |last=Hibbard |first=James |date=July 6, 2011 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |access-date=July 6, 2011}}</ref>

===Starring===
* [[Catherine Tate]] as [[Nellie Bertram]], the president of Sabre's special projects, who later usurps Andy's role as regional manager.
* [[Leslie David Baker]] as Stanley Hudson, a grumpy salesman.
* [[Brian Baumgartner]] as [[Kevin Malone]], a dim-witted accountant, who is based on Keith Bishop.
* [[Creed Bratton]] as Creed Bratton, the office's strange quality assurance officer.
* [[Kate Flannery]] as Meredith Palmer, the [[Promiscuity|promiscuous]] supplier relations representative.
* [[Mindy Kaling]] as [[Kelly Kapoor]], the pop-culture obsessed customer service representative.
* [[Ellie Kemper]] as [[Erin Hannon]], the receptionist and love interest of Andy.
* [[Angela Kinsey]] as [[Angela Martin]], a judgemental accountant.
* [[Paul Lieberstein]] as Toby Flenderson, the sad-eyed human resources representative.
* [[Oscar Nunez]] as [[Oscar Martinez (The Office)|Oscar Martinez]], an intelligent accountant, who is also gay.
* [[Craig Robinson (actor)|Craig Robinson]] as Darryl Philbin, the warehouse manager.
* [[Phyllis Smith]] as Phyllis Vance, a motherly saleswoman.
* [[Zach Woods]] as Gabe Lewis, the director of Sabre sales.

===Recurring===
* [[Mark Proksch]] as Nate Nickerson, a warehouse worker.
* [[Ameenah Kaplan]] as Val Johnson, a warehouse worker and Darryl's love interest.
* [[Hugh Dane]] as Hank Tate, the building's security guard.
* [[Lindsey Broad]] as Cathy Simms, a temporary worker.
* Eleanor Seigler as Jessica, Andy's girlfriend.
* [[Jack Coleman (actor)|Jack Coleman]] as Robert Lipton, a state senator and Angela's husband.
* [[David Koechner]] as Todd Packer, a rude and offensive employee, now working in Florida after Dwight and Jim [[Todd Packer (The Office)|tried to get him fired]].
* [[Georgia Engel]] as Irene, an old woman from Florida.
* [[Andy Buckley]] as [[David Wallace (The Office)|David Wallace]], the former CFO of Dunder Mifflin.

===Notable guests===
* [[Stephen Collins]] as Walter Bernard Sr., Andy's father.
* [[Josh Groban]] as Walter Bernard Jr., Andy's brother.
* [[Dee Wallace]] as Ellen Bernard, Andy's mother.
* [[Maura Tierney]] as Susan California, Robert's wife.
* [[Brett Gelman]] as an unnamed magician that Pam hires for Nellie's welcome party.
* [[Sendhil Ramamurthy]] as Ravi, a pediatric surgeon and Kelly's new boyfriend.
* [[Chris Bauer]] as Harry Jannerone, a salesman from the [[Syracuse, New York]] branch.
* [[Dan Castellaneta]] as Mr. Ramish, the CEO of Prestige Direct.

==Reception==

===Ratings===

{{image frame
|content={{#chart:OfficeUS8ratings.chart}}
|width = 500
|caption = Ratings for each episode of ''The Office'' that aired this season.{{ref|cite|i}}
}}

The series aired on Thursdays at 9:00&nbsp;p.m. on NBC.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2011/05/15/nbc-unveils-fall-primetime-schedule-for-2011-12-season-407413/20110515nbc01/|title=NBC Unveils Fall Primetime Schedule for 2011–12 Season|publisher=NBC|date=May 15, 2011|access-date=June 20, 2011}}</ref> The season premiere, "[[The List (The Office)|The List]]" received a 3.9/10 percent share in the Nielsen ratings among viewers aged 18 to 49, meaning that 3.9 percent of viewers aged 18 to 49 watched the episode, and 10 percent of viewers watching television at the time watched the episode.<ref name="ep01ratings"/> "[[The List (The Office)|The List]]" was the highest-rated episode of the season.<ref name="ep01ratings"/> Despite this, it became the lowest-rated season premiere of the series since the [[Pilot (The Office)|series premiere]].<ref name="ep01ratings"/> The rest of the season was unable to receive more than seven million viewers. The twenty-second episode, "[[Fundraiser (The Office)|Fundraiser]]", received only 4.17 million viewers, making it, at the time, the lowest-rated episode of ''The Office'' to ever air (although it was later beaten by several ninth-season episodes the following year).<ref name="fundraiser"/> The season finale, "[[Free Family Portrait Studio]]", was viewed by 4.49 million viewers, making it the lowest finale for ''The Office'' to air, beating the first-season finale "[[Hot Girl (The Office)|Hot Girl]]", which was viewed by 4.8 million viewers.<ref name="family"/><ref name=hotpressrelease>{{cite web |title=May 3, 2005 Press Release ("Hot Girl")|url= http://www.nbcumv.com/release_detail.nbc/entertainment-20050503000000-ahotmondaywithm.html |publisher=NBC|date=February 27, 2007|access-date=January 24, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081018000000/http://www.nbcumv.com/release_detail.nbc/entertainment-20050503000000-ahotmondaywithm.html|archive-date=October 18, 2008}} [http://www.officetally.com/the-office-nielsen-ratings/4 Alt URL]</ref> The drop in ratings led to a lower ad-price for the series, with an average cost of $178,840 per 30-second commercial.<ref name="ads">{{cite web|last=Steinberg |first=Brian |url=http://adage.com/article/mediaworks/chart-american-idol-nfl-duke-priciest-tv-spot/230547/#thurs |title=Chart: 'American Idol,' NFL Duke it out for Priciest TV Spot |work=[[Advertising Age]] |date=October 24, 2011 |access-date=October 30, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130516155932/http://adage.com/abstract?article_id=230547|archive-date=May 16, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> Despite this, the show was still one of NBC's highest-rated shows and ranked as the most expensive ad-cost for any NBC scripted series during the year it aired.<ref name="ads"/> Despite the lower live ratings, Nielsen Soundscan announced that ''The Office'' added up to 44 percent to its next-day "live plus same day" 18–49 rating when additional time-shifted viewing was added, such as [[Digital video recorder|DVRing]].<ref name=superbowl>{{cite web|last=Seldmen |first=Robert |title=NBC's Record-Breaking Super Bowl XLVI and 'The Voice' Supercharge the Network's Top-Rated Week of Jan. 30-Feb. 5 |url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2012/02/07/nbcs-record-breaking-super-bowl-xlvi-and-the-voice-supercharge-the-networks-top-rated-week-of-jan-30-feb-5/119061/ |publisher=[[TV by the Numbers]] |date=February 7, 2012 |access-date=February 9, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120213041035/http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2012/02/07/nbcs-record-breaking-super-bowl-xlvi-and-the-voice-supercharge-the-networks-top-rated-week-of-jan-30-feb-5/119061/ |archive-date=February 13, 2012 }}</ref>

The season ranked as the eighty-seventh-most watched television series during the 2011–12 season, with an average of 6.506 million viewers.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gorman |first=Bill |url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2012/05/24/complete-list-of-2011-12-season-tv-show-viewership-sunday-night-football-tops-followed-by-american-idol-ncis-dancing-with-the-stars/135785/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120527223446/http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2012/05/24/complete-list-of-2011-12-season-tv-show-viewership-sunday-night-football-tops-followed-by-american-idol-ncis-dancing-with-the-stars/135785/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 27, 2012 |title=Complete List Of 2011–12 Season TV Show Viewership: 'Sunday Night Football' Tops, Followed By 'American Idol,' 'NCIS' & 'Dancing With The Stars' |publisher=[[TV by the Numbers]] |date=May 24, 2012 |access-date=May 25, 2012}}</ref> The season also ranked as the thirty-second-most watched television series in the 18- to 49-year-old demographic. In this category, the show was viewed by an estimated 4.376 million viewers per episode and received a 3.42 rating/9 percent share among adults between 18 and 49. This means that, on average, the season was viewed by 3.42 percent of all 18- to 49-year-olds, and 9 percent of all 18- to 49-year-olds watching television at the time of the broadcast.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gorman|first=Bill|title=Complete List Of 2011–12 Season TV Show Ratings: 'Sunday Night Football' Tops, Followed By 'American Idol,' 'The Voice' & 'Modern Family'|url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2012/05/24/final-list-of-2011-12-season-tv-show-ratings-sunday-night-football-tops-followed-by-american-idol-the-voice-modern-family/135747/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525183657/http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2012/05/24/final-list-of-2011-12-season-tv-show-ratings-sunday-night-football-tops-followed-by-american-idol-the-voice-modern-family/135747/|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 25, 2012|publisher=[[TV by the Numbers]]|access-date=May 27, 2012|date=May 24, 2012}}</ref>

===Critical response===
[[Image:EdHelmsJune09.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Ed Helms]] received mixed reviews for his portrayal of Andy Bernard|alt=The image is of Ed Helms. He is standing outside and smiling at the camera.]]
The eighth season of ''The Office'' received mixed reviews. While some critics felt that the show was still humorous in its eighth year, many others argued that the program should have ended after the departure of [[Steve Carell]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.michigandaily.com/arts/notebook |title='The Office' Should Punch Out with Carell |work=[[The Michigan Daily]] |date=September 5, 2011 |access-date=November 6, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aoltv.com/2011/02/28/five-popular-shows-that-should-end-this-season/ |title=Five Popular Shows That Should End This Season |publisher=AOL TV |date=February 28, 2011 |access-date=November 6, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221100028/http://www.aoltv.com/2011/02/28/five-popular-shows-that-should-end-this-season/ |archive-date=February 21, 2015 }}</ref> ''[[The A.V. Club]]'' reviewer Myles McNutt criticized Robert California's role, noting that he is a character that "the narrative reacts to as opposed to something actually involved in the narrative".<ref name="av">{{cite news|last=McNutt|first=Myles|date=September 3, 2011|title=Doomsday|url=https://www.avclub.com/the-office-doomsday-1798170301|newspaper=[[The A.V. Club]]|access-date=November 4, 2011}}</ref> [[Alan Sepinwall]] of [[HitFix]] criticized Ed Helms' comedic performance as manager (calling him "a softer version of Michael Scott"), as well as the toning down of Robert California from his appearance in the show's seventh season's finale, "[[Search Committee]]". Sepinwall also expressed disappointment that many of the supporting characters were seemingly [[Flanderization|transformed into mere caricatures]] of their former selves.<ref name="hitfixeightreview">{{cite web|last=Sepinwall|first=Alan|title=Review: 'The Office' Struggles to Find its Center Post-Steve Carell|url=https://uproxx.com/sepinwall/review-the-office-struggles-to-find-its-center-post-steve-carell/|date=November 10, 2011|publisher=Uproxx|access-date=April 6, 2012}}</ref> He stopped reviewing a majority of the Season 8 episodes since "Pam's Replacement", due to his distaste for the series.<ref name="hitfixeightreview"/> ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' writer [[James Poniewozik]] also criticized the choice of Andy as manager, instead arguing that Jim should have gotten the job so the series could have been more ensemble-oriented.<ref name="time">{{cite magazine|last=Poniewozik|first=James|url=https://entertainment.time.com/2011/11/10/the-office-after-michael-whos-in-charge-here/|title=The Office After Michael: Who's In Charge Here? |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |date=November 10, 2011 |access-date=November 10, 2011}}</ref> ''[[New York (magazine)|New York]]'' named Andy Bernard one of the most annoying TV characters of 2011.<ref>{{cite web|last=Paskin |first=Willa |url=https://nymag.com/daily/entertainment/2011/12/tvs-ten-most-annoying-characters.html#photo=4x00002 |title=TV's Ten Most Annoying Characters&nbsp;– Vulture |work=[[New York (magazine)|New York]] |date=December 5, 2011 |access-date=December 7, 2011}}</ref> Early during the season's airing, Matt Zoller Seitz of ''[[Salon.com|Salon]]'' wrote a review in which he called the post-Michael Scott era of ''The Office'' "warmer and more reflective".<ref name="salon">{{cite web|url=http://www.salon.com/2011/11/03/the_zen_of_robert_california/|title=The Zen of Robert California|work=Salon.com|first=Matt|last=Zoller Seitz|date=November 3, 2011|access-date=November 5, 2011}}</ref> After the season finished airing, however, Seitz penned another review, writing: "Fact is, the show's first post-Steve Carell year has been a mess, at times bordering on a disaster".<ref name=disaster>{{cite web|last=Seitz|first=Matt|title=TV Review: Was Season 8 of The Office a Total Disaster?|url=https://www.vulture.com/2012/05/was-season-8-of-the-office-a-total-disaster.html?imw=Y|publisher=Vulture|access-date=May 11, 2012|date=May 11, 2012}}</ref> McNutt gave the season a "C" grade overall, writing that the season finale, "Free Family Portrait Studio" was "a disheartening conclusion to the show's worst season, offering little optimism to sustain our already dwindling enthusiasm over the summer months."<ref name=avseason>{{cite news|last=McNutt|first=Myles|title=Free Family Portrait Studio|url=https://www.avclub.com/the-office-free-family-portrait-studio-1798172769|newspaper=[[The A.V. Club]]|access-date=May 11, 2012|date=May 11, 2012}}</ref>

Bret Fetzer of [[Amazon (company)|Amazon.com]] wrote that "it's best to approach this season as if it were a completely new series".<ref name=amazon.com/> He felt that it is unfair to compare the quality of this season to that of past seasons because "the series' previous heights were so very high".<ref name=amazon.com/> However, he called the year "uneven", because episodes would range from putting "Andy into Michael Scott-ish situations" to "seek[ing] out new angles on the well-established web of interpersonal conflicts". This vacillation between extremes meant that the episodes "sometimes" work.<ref name=amazon.com>{{cite web|last=Fetzer|first=Bret|title=The Office: Season Eight|website=Amazon|url=https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0053O8AAK/|access-date=September 2, 2013}}</ref> Hank Stuever of ''[[The Washington Post]]'' named the series the tenth-best series of 2011, specifically praising the actors' ability in "Mrs. California" to deliver [[cringe humor]] without Carell.<ref>{{cite news|last=Struever |first=Hank |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/style/hank-stuevers-10-best-and-1-worst-tv-shows-of-2011/2011/12/07/gIQAEIGtfO_gallery.html#photo=1 |title=Hank Stuever's 10 Best (And 1 Worst) TV Shows of 2011 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=December 11, 2011}}</ref> ''TV Guide'' named it an honorable mention on their list of the best TV shows of 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tvguide.com/special/best-of-year-2011/PhotoGallery/Best-Year-TV-1039885#1040683 |title=The Best TV Shows of 2011 |work=TV Guide |access-date=December 15, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120106230627/http://www.tvguide.com/special/best-of-year-2011/photogallery/Best-Year-TV-1039885 |archive-date=January 6, 2012 }}</ref> Price Peterson from [[TV.com]] called the series "still one of the best shows on TV" and argued that, while "Season 8 definitely wasn't the show's best", the season "sneaked in some genuinely great jokes, new characters, and affecting plotlines."<ref>{{cite web|last=Peterson|first=Price|title=Looking Back on The Office Season 8: C'mon Guys, It Wasn't That Bad|url=http://www.tv.com/news/looking-back-on-the-office-season-8-cmon-guys-it-wasnt-that-bad-28698/|publisher=[[TV.com]]|access-date=June 22, 2012|date=May 17, 2012|archive-date=May 20, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120520120829/http://www.tv.com/news/looking-back-on-the-office-season-8-cmon-guys-it-wasnt-that-bad-28698/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Despite the lackluster reviews many of the episodes received, many critics praised [[Ellie Kemper]]'s performance as Erin Hannon. McNutt noted that "regardless of how down I was on this or any other episode, Ellie Kemper really has been tremendous all season."<ref name=avclub>{{cite web|last=Myles|first=McNutt|title=Tallahassee|url=https://www.avclub.com/the-office-tallahassee-1798171598|work=The A.V. Club|date=February 16, 2012|access-date=February 17, 2012}}</ref> In addition, Kemper's performance in the episodes "[[Spooked (The Office)|Spooked]],"<ref name="nationalpost">{{cite web |last=Hertz |first=Barry |url=https://nationalpost.com/entertainment/recap-the-office-season-8-episode-5 |title=The Office, Season 8, Episode 5: Recap |work=[[National Post]] |date=October 28, 2011 |access-date=October 29, 2011 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130104055904/http://arts.nationalpost.com/2011/10/28/recap-the-office-season-8-episode-5/ |archive-date=January 4, 2013 }}</ref><ref name="avclubspooked">{{cite web|last=McNutt |first=Myles |url=https://www.avclub.com/the-office-spooked-1798170192 |title=Spooked |work=[[The A.V. Club]] |date=October 27, 2011 |access-date=October 29, 2011}}</ref> "[[Christmas Wishes (The Office)|Christmas Wishes]],"<ref name="avclubxmas">{{cite web|last=McNutt |first=Myles |url=https://www.avclub.com/the-office-christmas-wishes-1798170784 |title=Christmas Wishes |work=[[The A.V. Club]] |date=December 8, 2011 |access-date=December 8, 2011}}</ref> "[[Pool Party (The Office)|Pool Party]],"<ref>{{cite web|last=Mader|first=Jill|title=The Office&nbsp;– Episode 8–12 Review&nbsp;– "A Party To Remember"|url=http://insidepulse.com/2012/01/20/the-office-episode-8-12-review-a-party-to-remember/|publisher=InsidePulse|date=January 20, 2012|access-date=February 17, 2012}}</ref> and "[[Special Project]],"<ref name="newyork">{{cite web|last=Tedder |first=Michael |url=https://nymag.com/daily/entertainment/2012/02/office-recap-season-8-episode-14.html |title=The Office Recap: Florida Facts |work=[[New York (magazine)|New York]] |date=February 10, 2012 |access-date=February 10, 2012}}</ref> in particular, were praised by critics.

In retrospect, many cast and crew members felt that the season was not the show's best. Rainn Wilson said that the season made some mistakes "creatively"; for instance, he argued that the chemistry between Spader and Helms was "a bit dark" and that the show should have gone for a "brighter and more energized" relationship.<ref name=ama>{{cite web|last=Wilson|first=Rainn|title=IAM Rainn WILSON&nbsp;– Dwight From the Office and the Founder of SoulPancake&nbsp;– AMA!|url=https://www.reddit.com/r/IAmA/comments/11isz9/iam_rainn_wilson_dwight_from_the_office_and_the/|work=Reddit AMA|publisher=[[Reddit]].com|access-date=October 20, 2012|date=October 16, 2012}}</ref> Brian Baumgartner felt that the show "stayed status quo [with the previous year], but without a key piece" and "didn't make a firm decision" on the direction it was headed.<ref>{{cite news|last=Justin|first=Neal|title=Q&A: Brian 'Kevin from The Office Baumgartner|url=http://www.vita.mn/arts/207619181.html|newspaper=[[Star Tribune]]|publisher=The Star Tribune Company|access-date=May 15, 2013|date=May 15, 2013}}</ref> Ben Silverman, one of the show's producers, said that "it didn't have the sense of purpose and focus" that [[The Office (American season 9)|the next season]] would have.<ref>{{cite web|last=Stanhope|first=Kate|title=''The Office'' Closes Its Doors: The Cast Spills on Spin-Offs, Steve Carell's Exit and Season 8|url=https://www.tvguide.com/News/Office-Oral-History-Steve-Carell-Exit-1065648.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130607043319/http://www.tvguide.com/News/Office-Oral-History-Steve-Carell-Exit-1065648.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 7, 2013|work=[[TV Guide]]|access-date=May 16, 2013|date=May 14, 2013}}</ref>

==Home media release==
The eighth season of ''The Office'' was released by Universal Studios Home Entertainment as a five-disc set on both Region 1 DVD and a Region A Blu-ray on September 4, 2012; a two-part Region 2 DVD release followed on February 13 and August 8, 2013.<ref name="region1a">{{Cite web|url=http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Office-Season-8/17111|title=The Office&nbsp;– Blu-ray Disc and DVD Announcement, Package Art for {{'}}''Season 8''{{'}}|work=TV Shows on DVD|last=Lambert|first=David|date=June 19, 2012|access-date=June 20, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120622020714/http://tvshowsondvd.com/news/Office-Season-8/17111|archive-date=June 22, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ezydvd.com.au/DVD/office-the-2005-season-8/dp/6137534|title=Office, The (2005) - Season 8: Part 1|work=Ezy DVD|access-date=December 7, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130217110533/http://www.ezydvd.com.au/DVD/office-the-2005-season-8/dp/6137534|archive-date=February 17, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ezydvd.com.au/DVD/office-the-season-8-part-2/dp/6142501|title=Office, The: Season 8 - Part 2|work=Ezy DVD|access-date=July 30, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307093603/http://www.ezydvd.com.au/DVD/office-the-season-8-part-2/dp/6142501|archive-date=March 7, 2016}}</ref> The set contains all 24 episodes of the season presented in a 1.78:1 widescreen aspect ratio with Dolby Digital audio and optional English and Spanish subtitles. The release also includes a variety of deleted scenes, "Producer's Cuts" of the episodes "Angry Andy" and "Fundraiser", "The Girl Next Door" webisodes, a blooper reel, and promos created for [[Super Bowl XLVI]].<ref name=season8dvd/>
